Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence—including both wake visual views—before proposing a single policy. I’ll also follow the fish-control bookshelf transfer protocol and keep its transferable invariant separate from task-specific details.

The parent examples all report the same capture at 0.7484 L, so the useful distinction is likely in trajectory and wake structure rather than headline score. I’m now loading the guidance lineage, inherited notes, controller contract, and the two required visual views for each sampled rollout.

I’ve confirmed the shelf is being consulted at the required architecture point. It frames mechanisms only; I’ll use a source only if its qualitative invariant matches the rollout evidence, and any adopted translation will be documented with an explicit falsification test in the notes.

The two complete-view rollouts show a self-propelled, coherent alternating wake and a stable S-shaped capture path; the blank lower rows in the other two are render failures, not contradictory flow evidence. Numerically, all four runs are trajectory-identical at 22.1540 T with mean distance 2.105583 L, while the recovery-preview variant is also identical—so that gate has no authority on this route. I’m isolating a new actuator path rather than retuning that exhausted predictor.

The candidate hypothesis is now specific: when the measured target line is still diverging on the requested side, reallocate a small fixed portion of the posterior carrier from the cancelling return half-cycle to the useful half-cycle. This preserves the traveling wave and existing mean-rudder ceiling; it tests sensor-qualified duty-ratio allocation rather than another lead or gain change. I’ll record that diagnosis and shelf transfer before touching the policy.

The policy and both required provenance files are updated. The new path is bounded to 0.05 of posterior carrier scale, activates only inside the inherited 8–5.5 L proximity envelope during target-line divergence, and leaves launch, carrier ceiling, and mean rudder untouched. I’m checking the contract and then I’ll invoke the mandated check runner; no CFD will be run.

The shelf transfer affected the edit exactly as recorded: the robotic-fish CPG invariant led to bounded, sensor-qualified half-cycle allocation; no published gains, clock phase, or route were imported. I’m now invoking the required check-runner configuration to validate guidance semantics, the Julia policy contract, and workspace boundaries without CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. The invocation itself was attempted; I’m executing the same three mandated checks verbatim and separately so the policy is still validated to the specified standard.

All three specified checks pass: guidance semantics, finite two-joint Julia output, and editable-boundary compliance. I’m doing one final offline replay of the new gate against the inherited trajectory—not CFD—to confirm it is neither a no-op nor active during launch, and then I’ll report the exact changed files.

Completed exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds bounded target-line-divergence posterior stroke reallocation. It is inactive during launch and capped at 0.05 carrier scale.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:286) now captures the recovery-preview no-op and inherited negative evidence.

All mandated checks passed: guidance semantics, Julia two-joint contract, parameter schema, finite output, and workspace boundary. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its three exact checks were run manually. No CFD was run.
